title: Protective effects of the FOXO3 gene in cardiometabolic disease in the Concord Health and Ageing in Men Project cohort.
authors: Abdi, Lovina; Lockwood, Glen; Le Couteur, David; Handelsman, David J; Naganathan, Vasi; Blyth, Fiona; Waite, Louise M; Cogger, Victoria; Willcox, Bradley; Allsopp, Richard
journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
one_liner_zh: 该研究为FOXO3基因变异与心血管代谢疾病关联的人群队列研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Recent findings from the Honolulu Heart Program cohort in Hawaii suggest a longevity-associated variant of Forkhead box O3 (FOXO3) may provide resilience against cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), such as hypertension, diabetes, and angina. The present study utilizes data from the Concord Health and Ageing in Men Project (CHAMP) cohort in Australia to further investigate the impact of the longevity-associated FOXO3 variant on CMD and longevity. Specifically, the protective "G" allele of rs2802292 was examined for potential protective effects against mortality in individuals with hypertension, diabetes, or angina (p-value: .01). Although no significant impact on mortality was observed in individuals with hypertension or diabetes, a reduced risk of mortality was observed for G allele carriers with angina. These findings are consistent with prior research linking longevity-associated FOXO3 variants to increased lifespan in individuals with heart disease and provide further evidence of its importance as a genetic factor influencing CMD risk. The protective effects against heart disease may arise from FOXO3's ability to enhance cellular resilience against oxidative stress and regulate metabolic pathways crucial for cardiovascular function. Additional studies are needed to fully understand the mechanisms behind FOXO3's influence on CMD, in particular heart disease, and to explore its potential for therapeutic development. This research highlights the relevance of genetic factors, specifically FOXO3, in CMD prevention and longevity in the elderly.
abstract_zh: 来自夏威夷檀香山心脏研究项目（Honolulu Heart Program）队列的最新发现表明，Forkhead box O3（FOXO3）的一个长寿相关变异可能对心脏代谢疾病（CMDs），如高血压、糖尿病和心绞痛，提供抵御能力。本研究利用澳大利亚康科德男性健康与老龄化项目（CHAMP）队列的数据，进一步探讨长寿相关FOXO3变异对CMD和长寿的影响。具体而言，研究了rs2802292的保护性“G”等位基因在患有高血压、糖尿病或心绞痛的个体中对死亡率的潜在保护作用（p值：.01）。尽管在高血压或糖尿病患者中未观察到对死亡率的显著影响，但在携带G等位基因的心绞痛患者中观察到死亡风险降低。这些发现与先前将长寿相关FOXO3变异与心脏病患者寿命延长联系起来的研究一致，并进一步证明其作为影响CMD风险的遗传因素的重要性。对心脏病的保护作用可能源于FOXO3增强细胞对氧化应激的抵御能力及调节对心血管功能至关重要的代谢途径的能力。需要进一步研究以全面理解FOXO3对CMD（尤其是心脏病）影响的机制，并探索其在治疗开发中的潜力。本研究强调了遗传因素，特别是FOXO3，在老年人CMD预防和长寿中的相关性。
